plateau_lod2_mesh — DRIVE japan op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.plateau_lod2_mesh(source: 'str | Path | bytes', *, origin: 'tuple[float, float, float] | None' = None, ids: 'Iterable[str] | None' = None, bbox_latlon: 'tuple[float, float, float, float] | None' = None, on_bad_polygon: 'str' = 'raise') -> 'dict[str, Any]' (to call the implementation directly, import driveplateau; driveplateau.plateau_lod2_mesh(source: 'str | Path | bytes', *, origin: 'tuple[float, float, float] | None' = None, ids: 'Iterable[str] | None' = None, bbox_latlon: 'tuple[float, float, float, float] | None' = None, on_bad_polygon: 'str' = 'raise') -> 'dict[str, Any]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("plateau_lod2_mesh"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Reads LOD2 buildings from PLATEAU CityGML and returns a triangle mesh (V, F) in local metric coordinates together with per-building attributes.

Streams bldg:Building with iterparse and treats the building body and each bldg:BuildingPart as one part (unit). Faces come from the lod2MultiSurface of the thematic surfaces (GroundSurface / WallSurface / RoofSurface / OuterCeilingSurface / OuterFloorSurface / ClosureSurface) and the surface type is kept in face_kind. Every face that lod2Solid references by xlink:href must be found. Holes (gml:interior) are bridged to the outer ring and ear-clipped; triangles keep the orientation of the original ring (outward normals).

Coordinates are moved exactly from EPSG:6697 (JGD2011 latitude, longitude, height) through GRS80 Earth-centred Cartesian coordinates into the ENU frame of the tangent plane at the origin (x east, y north, z up, metres). The default origin is the

ground centroid: the mean latitude/longitude of the GroundSurface vertices and their lowest height (all vertices if there is no ground).

fail-closed: an srsName other than 6697, an srsDimension other than 3, an unknown gml element in the LOD2 geometry (Triangle, OrientableSurface, pos point lists, ...), a thematic surface not in the table, an unresolved xlink and a measuredHeight unit other than m raise ValueError instead of being skipped.

Args:

source: CityGML text (starting with <), bytes, or a file path (str/Path).

origin: origin of the local frame (lat0 [deg], lon0 [deg], h0 [m]). If None, the ground centroid.

ids: gml:id of the buildings to read (the id of bldg:Building). If None, all.

bbox_latlon: (lat_min, lon_min, lat_max, lon_max). Keep only the parts whose mean vertex falls in this box.

on_bad_polygon: what to do with a Polygon that cannot be triangulated (zero area, self-intersection). "raise" (default) or

"skip" (counted in n_bad_polygons).

Returns:

{"V": (n,3) float64 [m], "F": (m,3) int64, "face_unit": (m,) int64, "face_kind": (m,) int8, "kinds": LOD2_KINDS, "units": [...], "origin": (lat0, lon0, h0), "crs": str, "n_buildings": int, "n_no_lod2": int, "n_bad_polygons": int, "max_nonplanarity_m": float}.

units[i] is {"building_id", "part", "gml_id", "measured_height", "attrs", "z_min", "z_max", "ground_z", "height_mesh", "extent_xy", "lat", "lon", "n_faces"}. height_mesh is

z_max − ground_z (the value to compare with measuredHeight); extent_xy is the ENU (x width, y width) [m].

Raises:

ValueError: the fail-closed conditions above, an empty or invalid source, broken XML, no matching part,

an unknown on_bad_polygon, or an invalid origin / bbox_latlon.

Examples:

>>> import driveplateau as PL

>>> m = PL.plateau_lod2_mesh(PL._citygml_lod2_example())

>>> [round(u["height_mesh"], 3) for u in m["units"]]

[12.0, 4.0]

>>> m["V"].shape[1], m["F"].shape[1], sorted(set(m["face_kind"].tolist()))

(3, 3, [0, 1, 2])
